title: Make Unix-only platform support explicit; remove dead #[cfg(not(unix))] exec_replace branch
description:
Portability inconsistency in src/lib.rs.

Current state:
- Module unconditionally does `use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;` (top of lib.rs) and calls `set_mode(...)` in `set_executable` and tests. These are Unix-only APIs; `std::os::unix` does not exist on Windows, so the crate cannot compile on non-Unix targets.
- `release_target()` only maps linux->linux and macos->darwin, and bails on any other OS. So even at runtime only Linux/macOS are supported.
- Despite that, `exec_replace` has a `#[cfg(not(unix))]` fallback (spawn + exit) alongside the `#[cfg(unix)]` `CommandExt::exec` path. Because the unconditional unix import already prevents non-unix compilation, the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` branch is unreachable/dead code and never builds.

Net: the crate is effectively Unix-only (Linux/macOS), but the dead non-unix branch and the cfg gating imply cross-platform intent that does not hold. For a reusable crate published with full crates.io metadata, this is misleading.

Recommended minimal fix (commit to Unix-only honestly):
- Remove the dead `#[cfg(not(unix))]` exec_replace fn and the now-redundant `#[cfg(unix)]` gate on the remaining definition, making exec_replace a plain Unix fn consistent with the rest of the module.
- Add an explicit "Platform support: Unix (Linux/macOS) only" note to the crate-level doc comment and the README.

Optional larger follow-up (defer unless there is demand): add real Windows support — cfg-gate the unix imports, provide a Windows set_executable no-op, and add a Windows release_target arm plus a zip-based asset strategy. Not in scope for this bead.

Acceptance: crate still builds + cargo test/clippy/fmt pass; no dead non-unix branch remains; docs/README state Unix-only support. Filed during overnight in-lane review of updatable-cli (board was empty).

title: Repo hygiene: apply rustfmt, fix clippy derivable_impls, add CI workflow
description:
The crate builds and all 16 tests pass, but routine hygiene has drifted:

- `cargo fmt --check` reports formatting diffs across ~21 regions of src/lib.rs.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` emits one warning: `AssetStrategy`'s manual `impl Default` can be derived (clippy::derivable_impls) — replace with `#[derive(Default)]` + `#[default]` on the `TendrilStyle` variant.
- There is no `.github/workflows` CI to guard fmt/clippy/test on push, even though this crate is intended to be published and consumed by other repos.

Scope: apply rustfmt, fix the clippy lint, and add a minimal GitHub Actions workflow running fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, and cargo test. No behavioural changes. Filed from updatable-cli dev session on operator 'continue'.

title: Private-repo support: attach token to asset downloads + optional gh-account token source
description:
Private-repo updates are only half-wired today. `UpdaterConfig.github_token` is sent as Authorization: Bearer only on the check_latest metadata request (lib.rs:224); the actual asset/checksum downloads in stage_next go through download_bytes/download_text which set User-Agent only and never attach the token. So even a correctly-authed caller cannot download a private release asset — it 404s. Confirmed bug, not caller misuse (kittui is wiring a stopgap).

Scope:
1. Thread the resolved token into asset + checksum downloads with redirect-safe handling that strips Authorization on cross-host redirects (GitHub -> signed S3 URL) so private downloads actually work.
2. Add an opt-in convenience for callers to source a token from the local gh CLI when none is set explicitly: new UpdaterConfig fields gh_account (Option<String>) and gh_token_fallback (bool), plus a gh_auth_token(account) helper running `gh auth token [--user <account>]`. github_token still wins; gh is only invoked when gh_account is set or gh_token_fallback is true, keeping existing public-repo behaviour and tests deterministic.
3. Builder helpers with_github_token/with_gh_account/with_gh_token_fallback and resolved_token().
4. Tests: auth header present on downloads when token set; auth stripped on cross-host redirect; resolved_token prefers explicit token without invoking gh.
5. README docs for private-repo + gh-account configuration.

Filed from updatable-cli dev session on operator request.
